verses.text: Then David ran away from Naioth at Ramah and went to Jonathan. He asked, "What have I done? What crime have I committed? How have I wronged your father, that he is trying to kill me?"
"Never!" Jonathan replied. "You are not going to die! Look, my father does nothing, great or small, without telling me. Why would he hide this from me? It is not true!"

But David took an oath and said, "Your father knows very well that you like me, and he has said to himself, 'Jonathan must not know this, or he will be upset.' Yet as surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I am only one step away from death."
Jonathan said to David, "Whatever you want me to do, I will do for you."
So David said, "Look, tomorrow is the New Moon festival, and I am supposed to eat with the king. But let me go and hide in the field until the evening of the day after tomorrow.
If your father misses me, tell him, 'David begged me to let him hurry to Bethlehem, his hometown, because a yearly sacrifice is being made there for his whole clan.'
If he says, 'Very well,' then I am safe. But if he loses his temper, you can be sure that he has decided to harm me.
As for you, be kind to me, because you have made a covenant with me before the LORD. If I am guilty, kill me yourself. Why hand me over to your father?"
"Never!" Jonathan said. "If I had the smallest idea that my father had decided to harm you, would I not tell you?"
David asked, "Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?"
"Come," Jonathan said, "let us go out into the field." So they went there together.

Then Jonathan said to David, "I promise by the LORD, the God of Israel, that by this time tomorrow or the day after, I will find out what my father is thinking. If he feels good toward you, will I not send you word and let you know?
But if my father plans to harm you, may the LORD punish me severely if I do not let you know and send you away safely. May the LORD be with you as he has been with my father.
And as long as I live, show me the faithful love of the LORD, so that I may not be killed.
And do not ever stop being kind to my family, not even when the LORD has wiped out every one of David's enemies from the face of the earth."
So Jonathan made a covenant with the family of David, saying, "May the LORD call David's enemies to account."
And Jonathan made David repeat his promise, because he loved David as he loved himself.
Then Jonathan said to David, "Tomorrow is the New Moon festival. You will be missed, because your seat will be empty.
The day after tomorrow, toward evening, go to the place where you hid when this trouble began, and wait by the stone called Ezel.
I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as though I were shooting at a target.

Then I will send a boy and say, 'Go and find the arrows.' If I say to him, 'Look, the arrows are on this side of you. Bring them here,' then come, because, as surely as the LORD lives, you are safe. There is no danger.
But if I say to the boy, 'Look, the arrows are beyond you,' then you must go, because the LORD has sent you away.
And about what we have promised each other, remember, the LORD is a witness between you and me forever."
So David hid in the field. When the New Moon festival came, the king sat down to eat.
He sat in his usual place by the wall, opposite Jonathan, and Abner sat next to Saul. But David's place was empty.
Saul said nothing that day, because he thought, "Something must have happened to David to make him ceremonially unclean. Surely he is unclean."
But the next day, the second day of the month, David's place was empty again. Then Saul said to his son Jonathan, "Why has the son of Jesse not come to the meal, either yesterday or today?"
Jonathan answered, "David begged me to let him go to Bethlehem.

He said, 'Let me go, because our family is having a sacrifice in the town, and my brother has told me to be there. If you are my friend, let me go and see my brothers.' That is why he has not come to the king's table."

Saul's anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him, "You son of a wicked, rebellious woman! Do I not know that you have taken the side of the son of Jesse, to your own shame and to the shame of the mother who gave birth to you?
As long as the son of Jesse lives on this earth, neither you nor your kingdom will be safe. Now send for him and bring him to me, because he must die!"
"Why should he be put to death? What has he done?" Jonathan asked his father.
But Saul threw his spear at him to kill him. Then Jonathan knew that his father had decided to kill David.
Jonathan got up from the table in fierce anger. On that second day of the festival he did not eat, because he was upset about how his father had shamefully treated David.
In the morning Jonathan went out to the field to meet David at the time they had agreed. He had a small boy with him.
He said to the boy, "Run and find the arrows I shoot." As the boy ran, Jonathan shot an arrow beyond him.
When the boy came to the place where Jonathan's arrow had fallen, Jonathan called out after him, "Is the arrow not beyond you?"
Then he shouted, "Hurry! Go quickly! Do not stop!" The boy picked up the arrow and came back to his master.
The boy knew nothing about all this. Only Jonathan and David knew.
Then Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and said, "Go, carry them back to town."

After the boy had gone, David got up from the south side of the stone and bowed down before Jonathan three times, with his face to the ground. Then they kissed each other and cried together, but David cried the most.

Jonathan said to David, "Go in peace. We have sworn friendship with each other in the name of the LORD, saying, 'The LORD is a witness between you and me, and between your descendants and my descendants forever.'" Then David left, and Jonathan went back to the town.
